chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī ibn Maʿbad, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Dihqān, from Abū Khālid, who said:

Wash all the dead: the drowned person, the one devoured by beasts, and everyone else, except one who was killed between the two battle lines. If there is still a remnant of life in him, he is to be washed; otherwise, no.

key_terms.أَكِيلَ السَّبُعِ: One whose body was eaten or torn by a beast.
key_terms.الْغَرِيقَ: The one who died by drowning.
key_terms.الْمَوْتَى: The dead persons whose funerary rulings are being discussed.
key_terms.اِغْسِلْ: Perform the ritual washing of the deceased.
key_terms.رَمَقٌ: A remaining trace of life or last breath.
key_terms.مَا بَيْنَ الصَّفَّيْنِ: The state of being killed between the two battle lines in combat.

ai.seo_question: Who among the dead should be given ghusl, and what is the ruling for one killed between the two battle lines?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding ghusl for the deceased. It states that all dead persons are to be washed, including those who drowned or were eaten by beasts, except the one killed in battle between the two lines, unless some remnant of life remained in him after being found.
